summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, chronic diastolic heart failure, and CKD stage 3, was admitted for diarrhea and worsening leg swelling with new erythema on the shins. The diarrhea resolved during admission and stool studies were negative for infection. Dermatology evaluated the leg changes and determined they were consistent with venous stasis, not cellulitis, recommending ACE wraps and elevation. He had one episode of hypoglycemia with a blood glucose of 56, prompting a reduction in his morning Lantus insulin from 30 to 25 units. He remained stable, with no further GI symptoms or signs of infection, and was discharged home with services. Follow-up was arranged with oncology and cardiology, and he was advised to monitor blood sugars and leg symptoms.
